author: reek
body: Connection lifecycle: a connection is kept open across requests (keep-alive), and when the client closes, the server completes the close and reaps the connection so the live set does not grow without bound.

author: reek
body: One client sends two requests on one connection, then a FIN. After the first GET the connection has served 1 and is still open; after the second GET it has served 2 and is STILL ONE connection (not a second) -- that is keep-alive. The FIN moves it to CLOSE_WAIT; the server sends its own FIN and removes it, so the connection count drops to 0. A server that opened a fresh connection per request would show two connections; a server that never reaped would still show one after the FIN.
